title: Nehemiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nehemiah chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nehemiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nehemiah Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem
The people blessed all the men
These are the chief of the province
Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib
questions.correctAnswer: The rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in the chapter, specifically in Nehemiah 11:1.

questions.question: Who blessed all the men that willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the people blessed all the men' in Nehemiah 11:2.

questions.question: How many valiant men from the sons of Perez dwelt at Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that 'All the sons of Perez that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men' in Nehemiah 11:6.

questions.question: Who was the overseer of the sons of Benjamin?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer' in Nehemiah 11:9.

questions.question: Which tribe dwelt at Jerusalem alongside the children of Benjamin?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that 'at Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin' in Nehemiah 11:4.

questions.question: How many men were part of the priests who worked in the house?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'their brethren that did the work of the house were eight hundred twenty and two' in Nehemiah 11:12.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a group of people that dwelt in the cities of Judah?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies the groups as 'Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants' in Nehemiah 11:3, but does not mention the scribes.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of the house of God?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Seraiah... was the ruler of the house of God' in Nehemiah 11:11.

questions.question: How many sons of Benjamin are mentioned in Nehemiah 11?
questions.explanation: The verse lists 'Sallu, Gabbai, Sallai' and mentions 'the sons of Benjamin' indicating a total of six in Nehemiah 11:7-8.

questions.question: Who was the second over the city?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Judah the son of Senuah was second over the city' in Nehemiah 11:9.

questions.question: Who is named as the son of Uzziah in Nehemiah 11?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions 'Athaiah the son of Uzziah' in Nehemiah 11:4.

questions.question: Is it true that the rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The text states 'the rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem' in Nehemiah 11:1.

questions.question: Is it true that the children of Solomon's servants dwelt in the cities of Judah?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'the children of Solomon's servants' were among those who dwelt in the cities of Judah in Nehemiah 11:3.

questions.question: Is it false that Nehemiah was the overseer of the priests?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer,' not Nehemiah, in Nehemiah 11:9.

questions.question: Is it false that the total number of valiant men that dwelt at Jerusalem was 500?
questions.explanation: The text specifies that there were 'four hundred threescore and eight valiant men' in Nehemiah 11:6, which is not 500.

medium.title: Nehemiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nehemiah Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many chief of the fathers are mentioned in Nehemiah 11:13?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:13 states, 'And his brethren, chief of the fathers, two hundred forty and two.'

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 11:14 promise will happen if someone participates in the work of the house of God as overseen by Zabdiel?
options: They will be mighty men of valor
They will be chosen to lead
questions.correctAnswer: They will be mighty men of valor
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:14 mentions that 'And their brethren, mighty men of valour, an hundred twenty and eight...' indicates those who serve in this capacity are recognized as mighty.

questions.question: Who was the overseer of the outward business of the house of God?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:16 states, 'And Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chief of the Levites, had the oversight of the outward business of the house of God.'

questions.question: How many Levites were in the holy city according to Nehemiah 11:18?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:18 states, 'All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred fourscore and four,' which totals 284.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 11:19 indicate about the porters?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:19 states, 'Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren that kept the gates, were an hundred seventy and two.'

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 11:20, where were the residue of Israel, the priests, and the Levites?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:20 indicates, 'the residue of Israel, of the priests, and the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, every one in his inheritance.'

questions.question: What role did Uzzi play according to Nehemiah 11:22?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:22 states, 'The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani.'

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 11:23 say about the portion for the singers?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:23 states, 'For it was the king's commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.'

questions.question: What responsibility was given to Pethahiah according to Nehemiah 11:24?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:24 states, 'was at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people.'

questions.question: How can the roles of Levites contribute to the worship in the house of God as seen in Nehemiah 11:17?
options: By leading in prayer and thanksgiving
questions.correctAnswer: By leading in prayer and thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:17 mentions Mattaniah as 'the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer,' highlighting the role of Levites in worship.

questions.question: Why is it significant that the Levites had oversight of the outward business of the house of God as in Nehemiah 11:16?
options: It limits their involvement in worship
It separates them from the priests
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:16 shows that oversight is vital for managing the physical aspects of worship, ensuring it is conducted with order.

questions.question: The people blessed those who willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem according to Nehemiah 11:2. What does this imply about the importance of willingness in service?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:2 indicates that those who willingly offered themselves were blessed, highlighting the value of willingness in service.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 11:15 mentions that Shemaiah is a Levite.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:15 states, 'Also of the Levites: Shemaiah...' confirming that Shemaiah is indeed a Levite.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 11:21 indicates that the Nethinims lived in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:21 states, 'But the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel...' indicating they did not live in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 11:6 states that all the sons of Perez dwelling at Jerusalem were valiant men.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:6 states, 'All the sons of Perez that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men,' implying a specific number rather than all being valiant men.

hard.title: Nehemiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nehemiah Chapter 11.

questions.question: In which village did some of the children of Judah dwell according to Nehemiah 11:25?
questions.explanation: According to Nehemiah 11:25, some of the children of Judah dwelt at Kirjatharba.

questions.question: Which village is mentioned alongside Beersheba in Nehemiah 11:27?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:27 states that some of the children of Judah dwelt at Hazarshual and Beersheba.

questions.question: Which two locations are mentioned in Nehemiah 11:30?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:30 lists Zanoah and Adullam among the places where the children of Judah dwelt.

questions.question: What is the last location mentioned in Nehemiah 11:35?
questions.explanation: According to Nehemiah 11:35, Ono is the last location listed in that verse.

questions.question: From which location did the children of Benjamin dwell at Michmash according to Nehemiah 11:31?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:31 states that the children of Benjamin from Geba dwelt at Michmash.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 11:36, where were divisions of the Levites found?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:36 specifies that there were divisions of the Levites in Judah and in Benjamin.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Hazar' in Nehemiah 11:27 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Hazar' means 'fortress' and is significant in the context of military and protective settlements.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Nehemiah 11:30 when multiple locations are listed?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:30 uses enumeration as it lists multiple locations where the children of Judah dwelt.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of settlement in Nehemiah 11:1?
questions.explanation: Ezra 2:1 discusses the return of exiles to their cities, similar to the theme of settlement found in Nehemiah 11:1.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of community in Nehemiah 11:2?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 describes the early church's communal living and fellowship, echoing the community theme in Nehemiah 11:2.

questions.question: What comes before Nehemiah 11:31?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:30 directly precedes Nehemiah 11:31, detailing more locations of settlement.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 11:26, which city is mentioned alongside Jeshua?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:26 mentions Moladah alongside Jeshua as places of settlement.

questions.question: The children of Benjamin are mentioned in which verse?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:7 specifically mentions the children of Benjamin.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 11:36 indicates that there were Levites in both Judah and Benjamin.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:36 states that of the Levites, there were divisions in Judah and in Benjamin.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 11:24 refers to Pethahiah as overseeing the Nethinims.
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:24 indicates that Pethahiah was at the king's hand concerning the people, not specifically overseeing the Nethinims.

theological.title: Nehemiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nehemiah Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 11:1 teach about sanctification in the context of communal holiness?
options: Sanctification involves separation and intentional dwelling in the holy city
Sanctification is primarily an individual, private matter without communal implication
Sanctification is only symbolic and has no practical residential implications
Sanctification requires abandoning all earthly possessions
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves separation and intentional dwelling in the holy city
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:1 describes the rulers and people casting lots to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city, showing sanctification as a communal and spatial separation for holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s providential governance is taught in Nehemiah 11:9 regarding city oversight?
options: God ordains leadership and oversight for order in His people
Human leaders act independently of God's providence
Leadership is unnecessary in a holy community
Only priests can govern cities in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains leadership and oversight for order in His people
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:9 mentions Joel as overseer and Judah as second over the city, indicating God’s providential arrangement of leadership for governance.

questions.question: What doctrine of priestly mediation and sacred service is highlighted in Nehemiah 11:11?
options: The priesthood is established as a divinely instituted mediator role over the house of God
Priests have no special role and are equal to all Israelites
Priestly duties are purely social and not divinely mandated
Only Levites, not priests, serve in God’s house
questions.correctAnswer: The priesthood is established as a divinely instituted mediator role over the house of God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:11 identifies Seraiah as ruler of the house of God, affirming the priestly role as divinely appointed mediators and leaders in worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 11:23 specifically demonstrate in the provision for singers?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:23 states the king’s commandment for daily provision for singers, reflecting God’s covenant faithfulness to sustain worship and temple service continually.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated by God’s ordering of Levites and singers in Nehemiah 11:22?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:22 shows God’s sovereign arrangement of Levites and singers over the business of the house of God, evidencing divine control over temple worship.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 11:18 connect to the theme of worship continuity seen in the Psalms and Chronicles?
options: It shows the restoration of Levitical worship as a continuation of Davidic praise traditions
It rejects Levitical worship in favor of prophetic leadership
It introduces a new, non-Levitical form of worship
It separates worship from the temple and priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the restoration of Levitical worship as a continuation of Davidic praise traditions
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:18 mentions 284 Levites in the city, connecting to Psalms and Chronicles where Levites conduct temple worship, showing continuity in redemptive history.

questions.question: In what way does Nehemiah 11:24 anticipate the messianic role of God’s appointed leader in redemptive history?
options: By showing a king’s hand in overseeing the people, it prefigures Christ’s sovereign governance
By establishing a purely human-led democracy without divine guidance
By forbidding any royal authority over the people
By emphasizing the priesthood alone as ruler
questions.correctAnswer: By showing a king’s hand in overseeing the people, it prefigures Christ’s sovereign governance
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:24 notes Pethahiah at the king’s hand in all matters, symbolizing God’s sovereign rule through a divinely appointed leader, foreshadowing Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Nehemiah 11:10 and Nehemiah 11:12 teach about priestly service and God’s provision?
options: Priests serve as mediators and are provided for by God through the community
Priests must sustain themselves without community support
Priestly service is optional and not regulated by God
Priests are only symbolic and have no real function
questions.correctAnswer: Priests serve as mediators and are provided for by God through the community
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:10 lists priests and 11:12 notes brethren who do the house’s work, together illustrating priestly mediation and God’s provision through communal support.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 11:15 and Nehemiah 11:16 teach about Levitical oversight and worship order?
options: Levitical leaders are divinely appointed to manage both spiritual and outward matters of the temple
Levitical roles are unstructured and left to individual discretion
Levites only serve in sacrificial duties without administrative roles
Levitical duties are temporary and non-essential
questions.correctAnswer: Levitical leaders are divinely appointed to manage both spiritual and outward matters of the temple
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:15 introduces Levite chiefs, and 11:16 details oversight of outward business, showing God’s design for structured Levitical temple management.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 11:4 and Nehemiah 11:7 teach about the corporate identity of God’s people?
options: God’s people are united in diverse tribal identities yet dwell in the holy city as one community
Tribal distinctions prevent any unified community in God’s plan
Only one tribe is chosen to dwell in the holy city exclusively
God’s people are scattered without any intentional dwelling
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are united in diverse tribal identities yet dwell in the holy city as one community
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:4 names Judah and Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem, 11:7 lists Benjamin’s sons, showing unity in diversity within the holy city community.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Nehemiah 11:20-21 shows a disorganized and unholy distribution of God’s people. What does Nehemiah 11:20-21 actually teach?
options: God’s people are intentionally placed in their inheritances with specific roles for Nethinims, evidencing divine order
God’s people are scattered randomly without divine purpose
The Nethinims are excluded from any holy service
The cities are abandoned and uninhabited
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are intentionally placed in their inheritances with specific roles for Nethinims, evidencing divine order
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:20-21 shows Israel, priests, Levites in inherited cities and Nethinims dwelling in Ophel under overseers, indicating God’s orderly distribution.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 11:14 teach about spiritual warfare and the role of the people in God’s kingdom?
options: God’s people include mighty men of valor who serve as defenders of the community
God’s kingdom requires no defense or valor
Spiritual warfare is irrelevant to the community’s life
Only the priests fight spiritual battles
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people include mighty men of valor who serve as defenders of the community
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:14 mentions brethren who are mighty men of valor, showing that God’s kingdom involves active defense and courageous service.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated by God’s provision of gatekeepers as seen in Nehemiah 11:19?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:19 describes porters and brethren keeping gates, reflecting God’s providential care in guarding His holy city and temple.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 11:31-35 contribute to the narrative arc of Israel’s restoration and fulfillment of covenant promises?
options: It shows the resettlement of tribes in their inherited territories, fulfilling God’s covenant promises of land
It shows tribes abandoning their inheritance and covenant
It depicts a failure to restore Israel’s territorial inheritance
It introduces foreign nations inhabiting Israel’s land
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the resettlement of tribes in their inherited territories, fulfilling God’s covenant promises of land
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:31-35 lists Benjamin’s towns and villages where people dwell, showing restoration of land inheritance, fulfilling covenantal promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 11:13 and Nehemiah 11:14 teach about leadership and spiritual strength within the community?
options: Spiritual leaders and mighty men of valor both contribute to the community’s strength under God’s guidance
Leadership is exclusively spiritual without need for strength
Neither leadership nor valor is significant in God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual leaders and mighty men of valor both contribute to the community’s strength under God’s guidance
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 11:13 lists chief fathers and 11:14 mentions mighty men of valor with overseers, showing a combined leadership of spiritual and physical strength.
